comment: Cases where the pyte pseudo-oracle genuinely diverges from xterm.js. These are pyte limitations/behaviors, verified by hand against the corpus bytes; xterm.js matches DEC/xterm documented behavior in each. The compare step exits 0 when the only failures are listed here, and exits 1 if a listed case starts passing (stale entry). This file applies to xterm-vs-PYTE runs; a real iTerm2 fixture run should start with an empty list.

divergences.reason: pyte has no alternate screen buffer: DECSET 1049 is recorded in Screen.mode but drawing continues on the primary buffer, so main-screen text stays visible
pyte has no alternate screen buffer: content drawn 'in the alt screen' bleeds onto the primary buffer and survives DECRST 1049
pyte does not implement ANSI save/restore cursor (SCOSC/SCORC, CSI s / CSI u); xterm.js restores the saved position
pyte does not home the cursor when DECSTBM (CSI r) is set/reset; xterm.js moves to (1,1) per DEC STD-070
pyte does not home the cursor when DECSTBM (CSI r) is set/reset; xterm.js moves to (1,1) per DEC STD-070
pyte does not implement SGR 2 (dim/faint); the pyte runner hard-reports dim=false
pyte draws a wide char whose second column would overflow into the last column anyway; xterm.js (like iTerm2) wraps the whole glyph to the next row
pyte does not implement SU/SD (CSI S / CSI T); xterm.js scrolls the screen/region per ECMA-48 and xterm
pyte does not implement REP (CSI b); xterm.js repeats the preceding graphic character with the current SGR attributes
pyte fills ED-cleared cells with the default background (it honors BCE for EL but not ED); xterm.js, like iTerm2, erases with the active SGR background
pyte leaves torn wide-char cells when one half is overwritten (the lead glyph or continuation stub survives); xterm.js blanks the orphaned half like iTerm2
pyte does not implement OSC 8 hyperlinks; xterm.js consumes them and reports linked cells as underlined through its buffer API (links render underlined; iTerm2 underlines on hover only)
pyte's NEL performs a carriage return only when LNM is set; per DEC, NEL is an unconditional CR+index, which xterm.js implements
pyte treats a DECOM CUP addressing a row outside the scroll region as a no-op (cursor unmoved); xterm.js clamps to the region bottom per DEC STD-070
pyte does not implement HPA (CSI `); xterm.js moves to the addressed absolute column
pyte does not implement CHT (CSI I) / CBT (CSI Z); xterm.js moves the cursor by tab stops
pyte's DECALN fills the screen with E but neither resets DECSTBM margins nor homes the cursor; xterm.js resets margins and homes per DEC STD-070
